title: Negation distributes over addition on the constructed integers
statement: `-(a + b) = (-a) + (-b)`. Route: `-t = (-1)*t`, `Int.left_distrib`, `Int.neg_one_mul` twice -- no case split on the two `Int` constructors. WHY IT IS NEW: the prelude HAD this proof and had never stated it. It existed as a private helper inside `int_prelude/modeq.rs`, built inline for `declare_modeq_add_right`'s cancellation step, with that one caller -- hiding place 2 in the retrieval taxonomy. `Int.sumRange_neg` needed exactly it, so the helper was widened and reused rather than re-derived. `Kernel::axiom_footprint` is EMPTY. Admitted by the trusted gate on the first attempt.

formal.statement: theorem Int.neg_add : ((x0 : Int) -> ((x1 : Int) -> Eq.{1} Int (Int.neg (Int.add x0 x1)) (Int.add (Int.neg x0) (Int.neg x1))))

evidence.supports: Int.neg_add is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.
